To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
organizational mindset shapes culture and employees’ perceptions and attitudes toward their organizations.
organizational mindset—whether an organization views talent as fixed or growth mindset—functions as a key belief that predicts organizational cultures and employee trust and commitment.

organizations that endorse a fixed (as opposed to growth) mindset have more negative organizational culture, lower levels of trust and commitment among employees, and are perceived by employees to have less collaborative, innovative, and honest cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether organizational mindset is associated with organizational culture, and how this association affects employees’ perceptions and behaviors.
the relationship between mindset and culture.
the relationship between mindset and culture and the implications of mindset for employee outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
organizational mindset is a core belief that functions to predict organizational culture and employees trust and commitment.
organizational mindsets shape the organizational cultures that in turn influence employees’ attitudes, trust, and commitment.
the mindset of a company is a core belief that shapes the culture of the company, which in turn, affects employees’ trust and their commitment to the company.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
organizations’ core beliefs about human potential shape their cultures and employees’ commitment and trust in their organizations.
organizational mindset shapes employees’ trust and organizational commitment.
organizational mindsets are a powerful predictor of culture and employee attitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizational mindset can be a key driver of organizational culture and employee outcomes.
organizations that believe in the malleability of talent will have a more positive culture and employees will trust and commit to these companies more than organizations that view talent as fixed.
the way a company talks about its talent shapes its organizational culture.
